- `eVe/elements/skin/index.js` is the canonical skin entry point for Dashboard, tools/toolboxes, and panel chrome tokens. It owns `EVE_SKIN_TOKENS`, `EVE_SEMANTIC_COLOR_FAMILIES`, `resolveEveSkinTokens(domain, overrides)`. Each semantic family provides a Dashboard `surface` and small-control `accent`; `default_values/constants.json` stores required family names rather than duplicate colors, and `dashboard_defaults.js` resolves them strictly. Domain modules may keep compatibility exports, but repeated color, opacity, shadow, backdrop, radius, size, spacing, and alignment defaults should be promoted into `eVe/elements/skin/` rather than duplicated locally.
- `SYSTEM_UI_THEME_TOKENS.surface` is the sole system-surface configuration. `resolveSystemUiSurface` compiles tint, background alpha and backdrop without fading text; `EVE_COMMON_SKIN_TOKENS.bevy.systemSurface` combines that paint with the existing exterior shadow. Dashboard, Matrix, panel/control and menu skins consume it. Panel shell and Dashboard header-band containers are transparent; body/footer surfaces own the paint. `systemContent` derives opaque white from the same central text tuple. No preferences UI or second style authority.
- Size factorization: `eVe/elements/system_ui_tokens.js` owns the one framework base unit (a square tool is `60 px`) and publishes `unitPx`, `halfUnitPx`, `doubleUnitPx`, `scalePx(referencePx)` and `eveCssPx(referencePx)`. Every drawn length of the UI lane is authored through that seam, so one base change resizes geometry, glyph boxes, text sizes, paddings, radii and shadows together: List rows and list columns are 1x (`60`), panel/accordion/contact rows, inputs, selects, segmented controls, numeric fields, scope chips, map result rows, calendar agenda rows and buttons 1/2 (`30`), Dashboard cells and Matrix tiles 2x (`120`). Gaps (`4-12 px`), the calendar time scale, non-row content blocks, gesture tolerances, viewport breakpoints, durations, map zoom levels, opacity/angle ratios and the single `999 px` pill sentinel are declared exceptions that keep their own proportions and still scale. `look/tool_theme.js`, `intuition/ribbon/tokens.js` and `atome/src/squirrel/apis/essentials.js` read that owner instead of their former `50 / 57 / 54 px` copies. Guards: `tests/eve/system_ui_base_unit_contract.test.mjs`, `tests/eve/system_ui_base_resize_contract.test.mjs`, `tests/eve/system_ui_base_wiring_guard.test.mjs`.
- Style factorization follows the existing ownership layers rather than adding a new theme module: `system_ui_tokens.js` owns the shared CSS backdrop and input text/focus depth values; `skin/tokens.js` derives its CSS/GPU blur projection from them; `panel_skin.js` owns one common backdrop material with domain geometry/shadow variants and one immutable panel-control state palette reused by actions, tables, Select, cards, summaries and inputs; `ribbon/tokens.js` projects the shared backdrop into legacy toolbox runtimes. `look/preset_{controls,chrome,comm_surface,comm_table}.js` compose repeated declarations from file-local definitions into independent preset objects so compatibility callers retain isolated mutable style records. `intuition/tools/visual/tool_visual_tokens.js` uses one selector-list builder for editor/footer tool variants and emits the shared tools declaration once. `tests/eve/bevy_panel_contract.test.mjs` guards the material derivation, aliases and explicit circular Mystic exception.

Should be extended by:

- Product-visible text through i18n keys only.
- Product design tokens and panel chrome behavior.
- New skinnable Dashboard/toolbox/panel domains through `eVe/elements/skin/` submodules.

Should not be duplicated by:

- Hardcoded visible labels in tools or panels.
- New local styling systems outside the existing design token structure.
- Parallel dashboard/toolbox/panel theme files that bypass `resolveEveSkinTokens()`.

Known risks:

- `design.js` is critically oversized and must be reduced when touched.

- `server/atomeRoutes.orm.js` owns authenticated event commits; `server/wsAtomeOperations.js` dispatches Atome WebSocket operations, `server/atomeRouteContract.js` owns boundary formatting, and `server/atomeSyncRuntime.js` owns sync side effects. The former CRUD/HTTP event route owners are retired.
- Sharing changes through the split sharing owners: message orchestration in `server/sharing.js`, ACL primitives in `server/sharingPermissionService.js`, and canonical Atome field accessors in `server/sharingAtomeAccessors.js`.
- Canonical sync delivery through `wsSyncRuntime.js`; per-principal cloud coffre
  lifecycle through `userVaultProvider.js`/`userVaultProcess.js`; routing and
  property projection through `userVaultRouter.js`; linked/manual/detached
  policy through `syncSharingService.js`; public invalidations through
  `directoryPublicService.js`. `wsSyncRuntime.js` also owns the per-connection
  serial control-message queue: subscription bursts preserve arrival order and
  cannot fan out concurrent replay IPC calls from one WebSocket. Batch
  subscriptions read access and heads through
  `userVaultRouter.authorizedStreamHeads` (vault op `stream:heads`).
  A linked share binds `userVaultRouter.streamForAtome` (vault op
  `stream:of-atome`, owner `database/adole_event_log.js#streamOfAtome`). An
  event's project (hence its `project:<id>` stream and `state_current.project_id`)
  is resolved from containment by `database/adole_event_containment.js#resolveEventProjectId`:
  a project atome is its own project; the client's current-project stamp only places
  a new atome with no known container.
  Tauri (`local_atome_containment.rs`) and iOS (`AiSRuntimeContainment.swift`) apply
  the same rule to local commits.
  Vault workers listen to their inherited IPC-channel disconnect and shut down
  even after an abrupt Fastify parent death; the provider bounds graceful stop
  and force-terminates an unresponsive owned worker after the timeout.

Should not be duplicated by:

- Browser-side REST/polling fallbacks or parallel communication systems.

atome/eVe OS image tooling (2026-10-30, development evidence only):

- `scripts/aOS.sh` delegates to `platforms/atomeOS/builder/core/cli.mjs`; the existing `core/build.sh` and stage scripts remain the only native image pipeline. `core/recipe.mjs` consumes the existing YAML configuration/profiles/packages and records committed source/submodule and builder hashes. `core/source.mjs` exports the application allowlist, `core/artifacts.mjs` owns source/archive/payload integrity and converted VM artifacts, and `core/remote.mjs` dispatches to explicitly provisioned SSH backends.
- `platforms/atomeOS/builder/installer/sbc/flash.mjs` is the shared PC/SBC macOS external-media owner: whole physical USB/SD identity, APFS boot-store protection, explicit numbered selection without a default, typed confirmation, identity rechecks, exact payload write/readback and ejection. `core/download.mjs` downloads an explicit HTTPS manifest/artifact with bounded size and integrity verification; the CLI's `prepare` composes build/download/local image selection with this same flash owner. No published release URL is assumed.
- `core/config.yml` declares live/installer mode support per target; `--mode all` expands only supported combinations. `scripts/configure_installer.sh` snapshots the real built system into a local distribution; `installer/desktop/install.mjs` verifies it and protects active GEOM ancestry before explicitly confirmed native `bsdinstall` partition/extract/EFI configuration. The installed `aOS-install` command invokes that same owner. No application UI, renderer, native audio engine or second image builder is added. Native installation, real download endpoints and physical-flash/boot acceptance remain unverified.
- Existing task/evidence owner: `todo/atome OS Audit.md`. `platforms/atomeOS/builder/docs/known_issues.md` distinguishes target recipes from build/VM/physical/production validation. Tests: `tests/governance/aos_builder.test.mjs`, `tests/governance/aos_installation.test.mjs`.

Mobile Tauri bootstrap and packaging:

- `platforms/desktop-tauri/bootstrap/` owns the minimal initial WebView document and bounded readiness navigation to the canonical local Axum runtime. Product UI remains in bundled `atome/src`; the bootstrap is not a second application surface.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/server/static_asset_cache.rs` owns the local
  Axum cache policy for bundled runtime assets. It applies conditional
  revalidation (`public, max-age=0`) to the root and eVe/Atome/source/vendor
  HTML, JavaScript and CSS routes while explicitly excluding `/api/`, `/file/`,
  `/text/`, and `/ws/`. `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/server/mod.rs` composes this middleware and must not
  duplicate its route classification or restore global `no-store` headers.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/tauri.conf.json` owns the iOS permission plist merge and the resource set limited to `atome/src` plus `eVe`; `platforms/desktop-tauri/tauri.android.conf.json` owns the Android overlay. `platforms/desktop-tauri/gen/apple/` and `gen/android/` are the generated native projects. The Android floor is API 29: `platforms/desktop-tauri/gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts` and `tauri.android.conf.json` must move together, because the NDK sysroot only ships `libamidi.so` (linked by `midir`'s Android backend) from API 29 onward, above the API 26 AAudio floor.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/Cargo.toml` keeps Reqwest on Rustls native roots for cross-target HTTP without a host OpenSSL link. Mobile debug builds resolve packaged resources even when Rust debug assertions are enabled; only desktop debug builds use the live repository path.

Browser-audio artifact compatibility:

- `platforms/web/audio-wasm/build.sh` builds only the browser Kira/Symphonia artifact with `-C target-feature=-reference-types`. Rust 1.95 otherwise emits WasmGC/reference-type descriptors that stable browser engines reject at instantiation (`invalid heap type 'exact'`). This scoped flag does not alter the root Rust toolchain or the native Tauri Kira build.

Verified desktop Bevy renderer owner:

- `platforms/desktop-tauri/Cargo.toml` declares optional Bevy dependency `0.19.0` behind `bevy_backend` and explicit renderer feature groups `bevy_renderer_core` and `bevy_renderer_native`. The repository root `rust-toolchain.toml` pins Rust `1.95.0`, which is the Bevy `0.19.0` MSRV and is required for `./run.sh`, Tauri dev, web Bevy builds, and direct Cargo checks. `bevy_renderer_core` enables Bevy WebGPU/window/winit/render/sprite/camera crates and the Linux `x11`/`wayland` Winit backends required when `bevy_winit` is active; `bevy_renderer_native` extends that core contract with standalone native-window extras such as `bevy/multi_threaded`. Renderer features do not enable `bevy_audio`, so Kira remains the single Atome audio engine.
- `atome/renderers/bevy-core/` owns the open Atome Bevy renderer core shared by browser/WASM and native/Tauri wrappers. It contains the Atome render DTOs/ops in `src/types.rs`, disposable ECS components/resources in `src/components.rs`, spawn/render-op projection, texture handling, render math, and selection overlay drawing. `src/render_math.rs` owns the fixed logical orthographic camera projection, and `src/render_ops.rs` reapplies it on surface resize so logical Atome geometry is not scaled by browser/window backing-buffer details.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/bevy_backend/mod.rs` owns the native Atome-to-Bevy backend surface. With `bevy_backend` it re-exports the shared Atome Bevy core and native power contracts; with `bevy_renderer_core` it also exposes the embedded native Bevy scene/ops entry point used by Tauri IPC. It must not become canonical Atome state, a DOM path, a canvas-per-Atome path, or a parallel scene model.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/bevy_backend/bridge.rs` owns the Tauri native Bevy command bridge. It accepts already-normalized disposable Bevy projection scenes and render ops from the eVe rendering runtime, starts an embedded `bevy_renderer_core` Bevy App with the shared Atome Bevy core, runs the Startup scene schedule without installing Bevy `WindowPlugin` or a nested winit/render loop from IPC, applies later render ops in native Rust, rejects ECS-only `bevy_backend` startup as non-presentable, and returns `presentable:false` diagnostics until a real native presenter is wired to the project surface.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/permissions/bevy-native-renderer.toml` owns the Tauri capability permission set for `bevy_native_start`, `bevy_native_apply_ops`, and `bevy_native_resize`; `platforms/desktop-tauri/capabilities/default.json` must include this set for the main webview so native Bevy startup cannot fail at the IPC authorization layer.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/bevy_backend/power.rs` owns the native Bevy power-policy contract. It defines `ATOME_POWER_PROFILE=eco|balanced|performance`, defaults to low-power idle behavior, keeps continuous/game mode opt-in, tracks explicit redraw requests, rejects idle transform writes without a dirty cause, and converts Atome power policy into real Bevy `WinitSettings`, `UpdateMode`, and `PresentMode` when renderer features are enabled.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/bevy_backend/renderer.rs` owns both Bevy App construction modes. `build_atome_bevy_embedded_app(...)` is the Tauri IPC-safe scene/ops engine and does not install Bevy window/render plugins; `build_atome_bevy_app(...)` and `run_atome_bevy_native(...)` remain gated behind `bevy_renderer_native` for standalone Bevy/winit presentation. Both modes install `atome_bevy_renderer_core::AtomeBevyRendererPlugin` instead of duplicating projection, spawn, or selection rendering.
- `platforms/ios/bevy-renderer/` owns the iOS C ABI staticlib wrapper around the shared Atome Bevy renderer core. Xcode builds it for iPhoneOS/iPhoneSimulator targets before Swift links, exposes `atome_ios_bevy_renderer_status(...)` and `atome_ios_bevy_scene_probe(...)`, and lets Swift report `linked_no_presenter` after Rust validates the native scene while the real native Metal/Bevy presenter is still being connected to the iOS project surface. The paired `platforms/ios/build_bevy_renderer.sh` build owner compiles this Rust staticlib with aborting panics, stripped debuginfo, and no forced unwind tables so the app and AUv3 Xcode targets do not overflow ld compact-unwind encoding with Bevy/Rust `__eh_frame` data. Normal Debug installs also use the optimized Rust archive; only `ATOME_IOS_RUST_DEV=1` selects the native dev archive.
- `platforms/web/bevy-renderer/` owns the browser/WASM Bevy WebGPU renderer surface. It consumes an explicit logical-coordinate `AtomeRenderScene` JSON/wasm-bindgen input plus DPR-aware surface metrics (`logical width/height`, `pixel_width`, `pixel_height`, `device_pixel_ratio`), binds Bevy to a caller-owned canvas selector, lets the browser/winit scale factor match the real DPR, treats backing-store resize signals as storage metadata, and keeps camera projection plus Atome geometry in logical coordinates through the shared `apply_surface` path. It uses WebGPU `CompositeAlphaMode::PreMultiplied` for transparent preview/capture surfaces and exports `run_atome_bevy_renderer(...)`, `apply_atome_bevy_ops(...)` for scene diff batches, `request_atome_bevy_redraw()`, the still-needed direct resource/text/surface/background/transform exports, renderer diagnostics, `read_atome_bevy_video_backend_capabilities()`, and video copy diagnostics read/reset methods without implementing a DOM renderer, canvas-per-Atome path, or fallback renderer. The video backend diagnostic uses schema `atome.bevy.web.video_backend.v7` to expose the live product backend as `gpu_external_texture_texture_external`, browser `GPUDevice.importExternalTexture` availability, and Web `wgpu` external-texture create/source/bind-group-resource support provided by the maintained backend fork while the blocker is `none`; it intentionally does not expose the deleted `video_track` API as a capability. Video-frame redraw notifications request Bevy redraw through the existing queued notification wake and no longer add a second post-application wake. `atome/renderers/bevy-core/src/video_diagnostics.rs` owns copy/skip counters for legacy/copy-pressure diagnostics only; it is not the active live project-video route. Supported browser projections now include Bevy sprite shapes, visible pending media sprites, Bevy RGBA texture sprites for text/raster images/SVG/persisted video posters/audio waveforms, and Bevy-owned live video mesh quads sampled from external browser video textures with per-track z-index ordering and canonical crop/UV mesh rectangles.
- `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_web_renderer_runtime.js` loads the generated browser Bevy module and wasm-bindgen binary from same-origin `/wasm/squirrel_bevy_renderer.js` and `/wasm/squirrel_bevy_renderer_bg.wasm`. It must not let the generated module derive the `.wasm` URL from a cross-port `import.meta.url`, because Safari blocks that CORS path before the project Bevy renderer can start.
- Live project video external-texture work stays in this same Bevy ownership chain: `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_web_renderer_runtime.js`, `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_web_presentation_runtime.js`, `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_surface_backing_sync.js`, and `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_video_decode_source_runtime.js` bridge browser runtime resources, strict canvas backing-store drift detection/synchronization, DPR-aware surface metrics, batched scene diffs, and coalesced frame notifications, `platforms/web/bevy-renderer/` owns WASM exports and web renderer integration, and `atome/renderers/bevy-core/` owns shared Bevy ECS/material/render logic. `bevy_surface_backing_sync.js` owns immediate backing synchronization plus the attribute-mutation drift guard; it must not reintroduce delayed timer repair bursts now that the web renderer receives physical surface metrics explicitly. `bevy_video_decode_source_runtime.js` applies derived timeline fields to the hidden source element before Bevy imports it as `GPUExternalTexture`, including trim seek, trim end/loop enforcement, offset, playback speed, status diagnostics, RVFC-first active playback pumping, and RAF fallback only when RVFC is unavailable. `atome/renderers/bevy-core/src/video_external_texture.rs` owns the shared ECS component, current extracted compositor layer, current per-track opacity, current normalized `uv_rect`, no-automatic-batching video mesh contract, and mesh helpers that rebuild UV coordinates for cropped source rectangles; `atome/renderers/bevy-core/src/video_external_texture_tests.rs` owns its focused Rust guardrails; `atome/renderers/bevy-core/src/video_external_web.rs` owns the browser `RenderApp` extraction/queue/draw integration, sorts external-video phase items by the extracted layer, and binds the per-video opacity uniform; `atome/renderers/bevy-core/assets/shaders/video_external.wgsl` owns the `texture_external` sampling path and applies color filters, transitions, and opacity as source alpha for the existing source-over blend. Local transform and crop projection flow through `AtomeRenderNode`, `AtomeTransformPatch`, `AtomeResourcePatch`, `render_math.rs`, and `render_ops.rs`; the old direct `AtomeVideoTrack` / `VideoTrack*` API and its WASM exports are deleted and must not be reintroduced. `atome/renderers/wgpu-web-external-texture/` owns the maintained `wgpu 29.0.4` / `wgpu-types 29.0.4` backend fork used by the web renderer Cargo graph to provide browser media source descriptors, `GPUDevice.importExternalTexture`, and `BindingResource::ExternalTexture` resource mapping. Direct JavaScript `GPUExternalTexture` probes remain diagnostics/reference only and must not become a second project renderer, hidden compositor, fallback, or canvas-per-Atome path.
- Browser/WASM Bevy rendering stays in the web-owned crate rather than the desktop Tauri crate, because the desktop crate owns Axum/Tauri/native dependencies that do not compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_native_renderer_runtime.js` owns the eVe-side native Bevy dispatch path. Browser mode uses `bevy_web_renderer_runtime.js`; Tauri WebView project surfaces use the visible Bevy/WebGPU canvas unless the host explicitly declares `window.__ATOME_NATIVE_BEVY_PRESENTABLE__ === true`. iOS/AUv3 project surfaces always select the native Bevy bridge when `window.__ATOME_IOS_NATIVE_INVOKE` is available, while the WebView remains the application shell and host surface. `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_native_texture_mapping.js` owns the native payload texture mapping for startup scenes and diff ops: image, text, and audio-waveform nodes are resolved through the injected shared media texture resolver before IPC when that native path is presentable, while live videos keep their source/external-texture route. Native mapping must not invent fallback colored media sprites or bypass the shared resolver for Bevy text/image payloads.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/AppNativeBevyRendererController.swift` owns the current iOS native Bevy command boundary. It calls the Rust staticlib status and scene-probe ABI so Xcode logs prove the shared Bevy core is compiled and linked, returns `ios_bevy_native_not_presentable` with `renderer_mode=linked_no_presenter` while the Rust/Metal presenter is absent, and keeps `presentable=0` diagnostics visible in Xcode. iOS must not silently use the browser/WASM main-canvas renderer.
- `setup.sh` and `scripts/setup/bootstrap.sh` own clean-clone setup for Rust/Cargo metadata resolution. They verify the Rust toolchain and resolve Cargo metadata without installing any global Bevy binary.

Verified iOS/AUv3 native owners:

As of 2026-10-09, the existing native media owners use iOS 17 rotation angles and microphone permissions, SwiftUI scene change actions, and registered size-class changes. Native iOS playback now runs in the shared Rust Kira engine (`AppNativeKiraEngine.swift`, 2026-10-14; the AVAudioEngine player is retired). Video inspection asynchronously loads properties/tracks through `AppNativeVideoRecorderSupport.swift#inspectAsset`; `AppNativeVideoRecorderTerminal.swift` publishes on the session queue only for the current lifecycle, keeps finalization active, and routes discard/error cleanup through the existing lifecycle owner. Public command/payload and renderer contracts are unchanged.

- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/FastifySyncClient.swift` owns authenticated
  `/ws/sync`, `/ws/api sync:push`, persist-before-ACK, and WebView notification.
- `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/server/local_atome_ws_sync.rs` owns the persistent
  authenticated inbound stream; `local_atome_sync_worker.rs` owns queued
  outbound `sync:push`; `local_atome_remote_projection.rs` owns local SQLite
  projection and cursors.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/FileSyncCoordinator.swift` owns file sync scheduling, safe-mode gating, tombstone state, move/deletion tracking, and the core newest-wins sync pass.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/FileSyncCoordinatorFileOperations.swift` owns visible/App Group/iCloud root discovery, syncable file inventory, file copy/delete helpers, and cleanup of leaked or duplicated sync artifacts.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/FileSystemBridge.swift` owns WK message dispatch, sandboxed path resolution, and bridge success/error serialization; `FileSystemBridgeJavaScriptAPI.swift` owns only the injected `AtomeFileSystem` JavaScript surface; `FileSystemBridgeOperations.swift` owns non-delete filesystem commands plus picker/import delegates and result forwarding — it routes the web layer's `photos` token to `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/PhotoLibraryImportPicker.swift` (the Apple Photos `PHPickerViewController` owner, which answers the same `{files:[{name,base64}]}` shape as the document picker) and its `*` token to the Photos/Fichiers source choice; and `FileSystemBridgeDeletion.swift` owns delete command adaptation. `FileSystemDeletionTransaction.swift` is the testable deletion transaction: coordinator/accessor/removal/absence failures escape before success, tombstone, or sync, while a partial batch marks only confirmed removals and syncs once.
- `tests/probes/filesystem_deletion_transaction_contract.probe.mjs` compiles and executes `tests/native/filesystem_deletion_transaction_contract.swift` to guard coordinator error, `removeItem` error, unconfirmed absence, confirmed success, and partial-batch tombstone/sync counts.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/MIDIController.swift` owns the CoreMIDI client lifecycle for the app (owned by `application/AppPageHost.swift`, started by the page's `start_native_midi`) and the AUv3 (owned by `AudioUnitViewController`, delayed start): one input port, each source tagged through `srcConnRefCon` with its `kMIDIPropertyUniqueID` (`coremidi-<unsigned id>`), UMP MIDI 1.0 channel-voice parsing, and the input list republished on setup/property changes (`WebViewManager.publishMIDIInputsToJS` → `eve:midi-native-ports`). The AUv3 also lists its host MIDI as input `auv3-host` (`auv3/utils.swift#parseMIDIDataDirect`).
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/MIDIOutputSender.swift` owns JS-to-MIDI packet output to host destinations.
- `atome/engines/audio/core/recorder/recorder_core.cpp` owns the native WAV producer/consumer lifecycle. Stop first closes admission, waits for every in-flight producer push, marks the producer drained, then lets the writer empty the ring before joining and writing the final WAV header; the last accepted render quantum therefore participates in `frame_count` instead of racing finalization.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/AUv3NativeRecorderBackend.h` / `.mm` own the Swift-to-recorder-core boundary, including exact written-frame totals plus overrun/discontinuity reporting; they do not define timeline placement.
- Idle output (iOS energy): the shared engine's `atome/engines/audio-engine/src/output_idle.rs` rests the device stream 5 s after the last voice (`retired:AppNativeAudioPlayback.swift` paused its AVAudioEngine the same way).
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/application/AppNativeAudioController.swift`, `AppNativeAudioRecording.swift`, and `AppNativeAudioRecordingScope.swift` own standalone iOS microphone capture over that shared recorder backend. The audio tap only forwards preallocated Float32 PCM, while the main-thread monitor publishes the shared 64-bin min/max plus RMS/peak scope contract through the existing native audio event bridge. After the recorder has closed a valid WAV, `AppNativeAudioRecording.swift` reads it in bounded Float32 chunks to return up to 256 persisted waveform peaks with the stop result; this finalization work never runs in the microphone tap or alters AUv3 capture. Playback and command routing remain split into `AppNativeAudioPlayback.swift` and `AppNativeAudioCommands.swift`; `ViewController.swift` only owns the WebView shell.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/AppNativeMediaCaptureController.swift`, `AppNativeMediaCaptureSupport.swift`, and `AppNativeMediaCaptureOperations.swift` own native permission routing, still capture, camera selection, and the generic video command bridge. They expose no native preview-layer command or recording preview surface.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/AppNativeVideoRecorder.swift`, `AppNativeVideoRecorderLifecycle.swift`, `AppNativeVideoRecorderSupport.swift`, and `AppNativeVideoRecorderTerminal.swift` own the serialized generic `AVCaptureMovieFileOutput` lifecycle. They coalesce concurrent stops, bound start/stop with watchdogs, validate non-empty positive-duration output with a video track and required audio track, cache unacknowledged terminal results for reload recovery, and make failed physical cleanup retryable. The bridge exposes `media_video_record_state`, `media_video_record_stop`, `media_video_record_cancel`, and `media_video_record_ack`; generic video is never labeled sample-accurate, and an exact request is rejected before state/camera acquisition.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/WebViewManager.swift` remains the shared manager/composition owner; `WebViewManagerScriptMessages.swift`, `WebViewManagerAudioTransport.swift`, `WebViewManagerNavigation.swift`, and `WebViewManagerIPC.swift` own script dispatch, audio/transport messages, navigation/media-permission delegates, and bounded IPC respectively. `FeatureFlags.panelLabEnabled`, `webInspectorEnabled`, and `textTraceEnabled` are false for normal Xcode launches and require their explicit Debug argument/environment opt-in; Release injects none of these diagnostics. Viewport sizing remains owned by the shared eVe surface lifecycle: the native bootstrap must not write document/body height or schedule delayed rotation corrections. This responsibility split preserves the same native invoke bridge and does not create another capture, transport, or viewport path.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/auv3/AUv3Recorder.swift` owns AUv3 recording session state, source start/stop, mic engine lifecycle, render buffer capture, and browser event emission. Exact overdub requires explicit `requireSampleAccurate`, uses only `plugin_input`, stamps `auv3.render` plus `record_start_render_quantum`, and returns the locked epoch, `auv3.host_transport` timeline origin, actual earlier playback start, same-quantum playback observation/recording start, frame count, strictly positive latency/offset, overrun, and discontinuity evidence. The separate `plugin` source remains generic output/mix recording.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/auv3/AUv3RenderEngine.swift` owns the render-quantum capture clock and the existing input-buffer handoff used by exact `plugin_input`; host transport sample time owns the timeline origin. No JavaScript timestamp may replace either native frame anchor.
- `platforms/ios/atome-auv3/auv3/AUv3RecorderAnalysis.swift` owns recorded WAV metadata analysis for peak and first-peak frame reporting after capture stops.

Verified desktop audio native owners:

- `atome/engines/audio-engine/src/recorder.rs` owns desktop recorder session state, CPAL input stream setup, capture callbacks, ring buffer production, and public recorder controls.
- `atome/engines/audio-engine/src/recorder_wav.rs` owns desktop recorder WAV output format selection, CPAL buffer-size hints, sample conversion, file creation, and writer-thread draining/finalization.

Should be extended by:

- Platform-specific native runtime boundaries, not product UI.

Should not be duplicated by:

- Browser-side filesystem or audio shortcuts that bypass the native boundary.

Known risks:

- AV phase has explicit pending work around Rust bridge extraction, CPAL callback disk writes, callback allocations, Swift debug paths, and legacy recorder FFI.

### Scripts And Tooling

2026-10-07 native build retention: `scripts/build_cache_retention.mjs` owns typed preview/deletion and active-owner deferral. macOS `run.sh` composes it at startup/exit with the existing Unix runner. `scripts/XCode_testflight_generator` uses standard project DerivedData; `platforms/ios/build_bevy_renderer.sh` shares the existing device Rust cache across configurations and targets. Policy: `scripts/build_cache_retention.md`; regressions: `tests/governance/build_cache_retention.test.mjs`. No application state or rendering ownership changes.
2026-10-18 workspace residue retention: `scripts/workspace_residue_retention.mjs` plans age-based deletion for the `scripts/build_cache_retention.mjs` owner (Cargo units by hash and access time, incremental configurations per crate, stale `temp/` trees with probe sources and `.retain` kept, agent scratchpads, superseded DeviceSupport). Regressions: `tests/governance/build_cache_retention.test.mjs`.

Path: `scripts/`, `scripts_utils/`, `tools/`

Owner: Development and validation tooling.

Purpose: Build scripts, setup workflows, syntax/fallback guardrails, Tauri boundary checks, Molecule guardrails, Fastify runner, static server, publishing scripts, and live smoke/probe suites.

Production service routing:

- `scripts/commit_and_push.sh` is the user-operated, interactive Git publication helper for the framework root and nested repositories such as `eVe`. It requires an explicit repository, commit message, and literal path list; refuses detached HEAD, merge conflicts, pre-existing staged changes, and targets outside the framework; displays the selected status and remote; requires an exact branch confirmation; and never force-pushes or mutates tags. Coding agents may validate its non-mutating help and syntax paths but remain subject to the repository Git read-only policy and must not execute its publication path.
- `scripts/setup/run_unix.sh` owns the early production-service dispatch point for `./run.sh --https`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, `status`, `logs`, `check`, `update`, and installed-production `--server`. These commands must exit before development bootstrap, dependency installation, local `.env` writes, SQLite/upload watcher setup, Fastify dev launch, or Tauri launch. On an installed production host, the no-argument dev path is also rejected before bootstrap so accidental `./run.sh` cannot install Tauri dependencies or run `npm ci`. Local `./run.sh --test` is a non-production development/test launch mode only; it exports `NODE_ENV=test`, `SQUIRREL_AUTH_TEST_MODE=1`, and `SQUIRREL_AUTH_OTP_BYPASS=1`, forwards `--test` to Fastify and Tauri child runners, is rejected when `NODE_ENV=production`, and cannot be combined with production build modes. This keeps explicit Debian test-server foreground launches available while production runtime/build paths remain closed.
- `scripts/setup/service_commands.sh` owns the production service command implementations shared by that early dispatch. Its production `--server` path is foreground diagnostics only: it loads the service environment, refuses to run while the service is active, and directly executes `server/server.js` without development setup.
- `scripts/android/apk.sh` owns the Android build lane, dispatched by `./run.sh apk` through the `apk` case of `scripts/setup/service_commands.sh`. It is the single owner of JDK/SDK/NDK/Rust-target resolution (idempotent: present and current means untouched, missing or older means installed, failure means a named error with no substitution), of `tauri android init`, of the staged `platforms/desktop-tauri/gen/android-webroot` frontendDist, of release-keystore creation under `~/.atome/android/`, and of every `tauri android build`/`dev` invocation. `--doctor` reports the chain without building, `--dry-run` prints the exact plan, and `--isolated-home <dir>` keeps the cargo, Gradle and Android user caches under `<dir>` instead of `$HOME` for hermetic and CI builds. Artifact discovery reads the CLI's own `Finished N APK at:` report, because AGP nests outputs under their Gradle flavor (`outputs/apk/<flavor>/debug/`); missing CLI artifact evidence now stops the build instead of substituting an older file, and the build log stays in the git-ignored `temp/apk-build.log`, and `--install` installs the verified list instead of re-searching for a file. The build log captures both streams, because that report is written to stderr while Gradle diagnostics go to stdout. `remove_stale_artifacts()` drops this build type's previous APK or AAB before the build, because AGP packs into an existing file without truncating it and a repackaged debug APK otherwise carried 489 765 844 dead bytes (994 683 526 bytes instead of 504 916 716). `platforms/desktop-tauri/tauri.android.conf.json` is the Android configuration overlay; `platforms/desktop-tauri/gen/android` is the Gradle project, kept in the repository so signing and manifest customizations survive; `platforms/desktop-tauri/src/android_assets.rs` owns the runtime materialization of the embedded web root. No other script may call `tauri android`.
- `scripts/setup/bootstrap.sh` owns clean-clone and development bootstrap only. It must not be required for installed production service management.
- `scripts/server_update.js` owns reproducible production update orchestration, including dependency reinstall, runtime-dependency verification, service restart, and Nginx reload. It logs each phase (`env`, `backup`, `systemd-unit`, `git-update`, `eve-source`, `verify-source`, `npm-ci`, `verify-runtime-dependencies`, `restart`, `status`, `health`, `nginx-reload`) with command, cwd, duration, and exit status, delegates production secrets and signing identity to `scripts/server_secure_config.js`, initializes and updates the required `eVe` submodule, verifies source immediately after Git/eVe update, and refuses to restart until the installed production assets pass runtime verification.
- `scripts/server_secure_config.js` owns production JWT/cookie secret preservation, persistent signing-key adoption/generation, stable server identity metadata, fail-closed pair validation, permissions, and pre-update identity backup. Generated keys live outside the Git checkout under `/etc/squirrel/identity`; a code update must never rotate them.
- `scripts/verify_deployed_source.js` owns deployed-source verification for production routing, `/eVe/` static serving, required `eVe/eVe.js` and `eVe/version.txt` assets, production secure-config and identity provisioning, and deployable dependencies. Lock validation is semantic: each runtime dependency must be declared by `package.json`, carry the same root request in `package-lock.json`, and have a versioned integrity-checked package entry; npm's incidental transitive hoisting layout is not a deployment contract. Its runtime verification requires the browser assets Fastify serves from installed packages, currently Rubber Band's ESM module and WASM binary.
- `update_server.sh` is the root production update wrapper around `scripts/server_update.js`, certificate renewal, deployed-source verification, final restart, and HTTP postcheck. Manual runs print to the terminal and append `logs/update_server.log`; `QUIET=1` is reserved for automation. Each run emits a `run_id`, preflight identity, phase start/end/failure records, current HEAD on failures, service postcheck output, and a final summary. Before certificate or dependency work it self-updates `/opt/a` from `origin/main`, stashes local changes that block a fast-forward pull, supports explicit `--reset` repair to force `main` to `origin/main`, and re-executes itself if the wrapper source changed. Certificate renewal is skipped when the existing certificate is still valid beyond the configured renewal window, so Let's Encrypt rate limits do not block dependency installation or service restart. Its verification step delegates to `scripts/verify_deployed_source.js`, which prints the deployed Atome and eVe Git identities and fails before restart if the production `--server` early route, `/eVe/` static route, required eVe files, or required lockfile markers are absent. Its postcheck waits for the configurable local health endpoint, then verifies `GET /eVe/eVe.js`, `GET /eVe/version.txt`, and `GET /api/server-info` so `eveVersion: "unknown"` cannot be reported as a successful deployment.

## Duplication And Cleanup Risks

Recent rendering and persistence fixes:

- `eVe/domains/media/api/media_persistence_service.js`: recording Atome reuse must commit the active `project_id` before rendering; reusing an existing `video_recording_*` / `audio_recording_*` without this association leaves project reload and list results inconsistent.
- `atome/src/squirrel/apis/unified/adole_api/atome_record_projection.js`: `state_current.meta.project_id` is part of the client projection contract and must survive reload into both top-level `project_id` and `meta.project_id`.
- `eVe/domains/rendering/project_scene_runtime.js`: Bevy projection must skip stale media records that have no renderable source; old source-less `audio_recording_*` records must not abort WebGPU scene startup. Reconciliation may restore a previous virtual scene as the diff baseline only when the previous projection was presentable (`projection.ok === true`); failed Safari/WebKit startup projections must force the next pass through a full Bevy start/spawn scene, even when Dashboard records are unchanged, so Dashboard entêtes cannot be skipped as already-present nodes.
- `eVe/domains/rendering/bevy_web_renderer_runtime.js`: initial Bevy startup and later spawn diffs record unrecoverable media texture decode failures as skipped nodes instead of rejecting the whole scene or diff batch; valid nodes must still start. Uncached video and audio-waveform nodes remain present as Bevy entities and receive textures later through one-at-a-time resource updates; video frame failures and blank transparent/black readbacks are retried with bounded backoff before being marked skipped, so Safari/WKWebView frame timing cannot make Atomes disappear or leave a refresh-time video permanently transparent after one early miss.
- `atome/renderers/bevy-core/src/render_math.rs` and `render_ops.rs`: layer depth is clamped for Bevy sprites, meshes, overlays, and source-backed video so timestamp-like z-index values remain inside the explicit Atome camera depth volume while preserving the canonical `AtomeLayer`; the clamp must remain above the eVe workspace layer bands (`dashboard`, `panel`, `mainMenu`, `mystic`) plus their local render-layer ranges so Dashboard card/media/label ordering is not flattened. Render-op transform/layer updates explicitly refresh Bevy transform components for extraction. Local transform scale/rotation/origin is derived from the canonical Virtual Scene payload, stored as disposable ECS `AtomeLocalTransform`, and reapplied during transform and surface-size operations without becoming canonical state. Camera projection is fixed to the logical surface dimensions, uses an explicit near/far range large enough for high Dashboard layers before any browser resize event, and is updated on surface resize; do not compensate with dashboard/project record scale transforms.
- Durable media cache reuse is owned by the existing projection path, not by a new renderer cache layer: `render_atom.js` exposes persisted video poster data URLs and waveform peaks, `bevy_media_texture_resolver.js` consumes persisted video posters only for non-live poster texture payloads, and `project_audio_waveform_renderer.js` consumes persisted waveform peaks before requesting metadata or decoding audio. Full RGBA/GPU textures remain disposable derived renderer resources.

High priority risks:

- Historical snapshot (retired owner; not current availability evidence): Oversized files: `eve/elements/design.js`, `atome/src/squirrel/ai/agent_gateway.js`, `retired:atome/src/application/jeezs/index.js`, `atome/src/application/audio_runtime/play_record_core.js`.
- Legacy naming overlap: `mtrack`, `mtrax`, `hmtracks`, and `Molecule` remain mixed pending the Molecule rename phase.
- Product bootstrap references still exist in Atome bootstrap paths and need architecture-map treatment.
- Direct DOM helper modules exist in eVe Intuition and need targeted policy review before UI expansion.
- Server ownership is likely open infrastructure, but exact product/open boundary needs explicit architecture-map verification.

General risks:

- Avoid adding logic to vendored/minified assets under `atome/src/js/`.
- Avoid creating new temporary scripts outside `temp/`.
- Avoid creating new maps under `docs/`; use `maps/`.

# Resident Dashboard lifecycle (2026-07-17, authoritative)

This section supersedes earlier Dashboard lifecycle descriptions in this map. The resident full-screen Dashboard tree was removed on 2026-10-24: `openWorkspaceDashboardAndMainMenu` (`eVe/intuition/tools/user_workspace_surface_runtime.js`) only opens the eVe home. Closing the Dashboard never calls `activateProjectWorkspace()`, `setCurrent`, project persistence, `loadProjectAtomes()`, preview capture, or a full scene render. The main menu remains mounted in the same scene, while contextual edit and video decode runtimes suspend from the existing workspace-mode event. Rounded-mask and shape-shadow caches are byte-bounded at 8 MiB each in `atome/renderers/bevy-core/src/components.rs`.

`eVe/domains/dashboard/dashboard_actions.js` owns the closed item-routing table: Projects delegate unchanged to `project_data.js#activateProjectWorkspace`, Calendar delegates by event id to its existing panel, Contacts delegate by stable identity to the existing Contact panel, and unsupported categories return inert without projecting a generic detail surface. It may not create a second state, panel, renderer, or persistence path.

# Dashboard interaction performance ownership (2026-07-18, authoritative)

- `bevy_ui_overlay_record_projection.js` owns BevyUI-tree-to-overlay-record conversion. `project_scene_direct_prefix_runtime.js` applies compatible palette prefix additions/removals and same-id visual changes atomically against resident scene records; `project_scene_direct_motion_runtime.js` applies later transform/style samples without rebuilding the Dashboard, re-normalizing render nodes, or re-hashing unchanged RGBA payloads. Both routes share the serialized direct-mutation queue and retain canonical projection as the guarded fallback.
- `bevy_ui_main_menu_runtime.js` keeps palette children absent while closed and prewarms only their image/label textures, one palette per idle frame, through the shared bounded texture cache without mounting or projection. Activation submits one complete opaque structural palette atomically at the expansion origin: every background, accent, tool, icon, and label exists before movement, with no delayed texture or opacity. Structural icon/label layout stays relative until projection; direct samples then move the tool, icon, label, accent, and displaced siblings together through the full 180/70/120 ms curve. `bevy_ui_main_menu_palette_motion.js` owns that one interruptible `requestAnimationFrame` loop, including the outward 6–14 px overshoot and exact settlement. Frame sampling never waits on a renderer promise: at most one WebGPU submission is in flight, and backpressure retains only the latest pending sample instead of building a FIFO, trail, or stale terminal update. The last motion sample is the definitive layout, with no redundant structural render.
- `platforms/web/bevy-renderer/src/lib.rs` owns Web presentation cadence with `frame_clock.rs`: wakes request one animation frame whose update drains the single per-frame operation batch (500 ms idle heartbeat for 3 s after the last wake, then 10 s; see the 2026-10-07 frame clock entry). `bevy_web_renderer_module_loader.js` reloads the tiny renderer-version manifest once per page boot, then content-addresses both wasm-bindgen glue and WASM with the binary hash so a rebuilt binary can never be paired with stale cached glue.
# Contact panel migration update — 2026-08-02

- `bevy_panel_contact_runtime.js` owns Contact orchestration and only ephemeral
  `expandedId`, `selectedIds`, one open draft, confirmation, import, and text-
  projection state. `bevy_panel_contact_view.js` projects one neutral shared
  accordion per stable identity; `bevy_panel_contact_editing.js` reuses the one
  hidden text service; `bevy_panel_contact_actions.js` owns the compact footer,
  disclosed transfer pane and contextual selection actions — including the
  `Create user` shortcut that hands account creation
  to the Home/login owner through `contact.create_user` — and delegates effects
  to the existing service owners. There is
  no selected-row list, blue state, check-mark header, or global editor.
- `contact_model.js` accepts and reconciles identities only through explicit
  `id` or `source_contact_id` values. Name, phone, and email remain display and
  search data and never authorize merging, editing, or deletion. The exact
  authenticated profile is projected once at the top and is editable only
  through `profile_api.js`; local `eve_contacts_local` entries alone expose the
  compact checkbox rail and grouped deletion.
- The shared `accordionNode`, `toggleableRowNode`, text inputs, action buttons,
  and fixed panel children remain the only visual builders. Checkbox pointer
  ownership supports a bounded vertical rail gesture; drag outside that rail
  remains normal panel scrolling. The rail and the custom-field `+` reuse the
  canonical 30 px icon-button surface; custom fields precede that `add.svg`
  action. An avatar is projected only when `user_face` exists.
- `connector_contract.js` and `service_contact_utils.js` expose the explicit
  `interactive_import` and localized `label_key` source metadata. The Contact
  panel filters on that capability, so CardDAV/iCloud stays headless. The fixed
  row above the shared footer is `Importer`, `Ajouter`, and conditional

- `eVe/domains/rendering/surface_runtime.js` is the only workspace-size observer and publishes distinct stabilized sizes through `subscribeRenderSurfaceSize`. Dashboard, main menu and structured project views subscribe to it and must not add viewport or surface resize observers of their own.

It records explicit intent before asynchronous surface work, checks the intent sequence again after persistence reads, and commits same-mode choices because the local-first in-memory default can differ from durable state. `project_view_records.js` owns canonical paged project reads, preserves `meta.project_id` membership, and excludes canonical deletion tombstones; `project_view_reorder_runtime.js` owns durable `hierarchy_order` writes and uses one canonical batch when available. The canonical shared drag session owns pointer preservation and drag cleanup; List renders a source fade plus insertion gap, while Matrix consumes the same press/drag/release lifecycle. `project_view_surface_runtime.js` retains a pending pointer-node preservation request across queued renders. List and Matrix rebuild their selected projection from canonical selection on load. `project_view_surface_context_runtime.js` owns the contextual rail and `project_view_surface_events.js` owns canonical change/size subscriptions.
- `project_data.js` owns a single global latest-wins workspace-activation generation. It starts the persisted-mode prefetch through `project_view_mode_state.js`, consumes the authoritative `loadProjectAtomes` projection, then calls that same owner's guarded restoration once after loading. The activation load carries internal `viewModePrepared: true`; `tool_genesis_project_load_runtime.js` skips only its redundant restoration in that case. A Natural/Matrix/List gesture after prefetch invalidates the old result and same-mode Natural is still committed, so a late restore cannot overwrite the user. Boot loads await the same single restoration before publishing project readiness; the authoritative refresh never starts a second one.

### iOS event journal latency and atomic projection (2026-09-11)

`platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/AiSRuntimeEvents.swift` owns event normalization, journal append and projection as an extension of the existing AiSRuntime, extracted from LocalHTTPServer. Each event uses a SQLite savepoint so journal, particles and state-current commit or roll back together; enclosing remote-sync transactions retain ownership. Sequential batches retain per-event semantics. Sequence allocation includes `sequence IS NOT NULL`, matching the existing partial stream/sequence index rather than scanning the journal. The executable Swift probe covers rollback, duplicate IDs, nested transactions and index selection. Physical iPhone startup: 453 events / 1379 ms cumulative handler time, p50 3 ms, p95 4 ms, zero observed local request timeouts; assistant network and Mystic acceptance remain open.

`platforms/ios/atome-auv3/Common/AiSRuntimeStateCurrent.swift` owns the state-current read boundary as the same kind of AiSRuntime extension, extracted from LocalHTTPServer: message handling, `get`/`list`/`count`, row loading and serialization, `canReadState` authorization, upserts and Atome-meta lookup. It also owns the single read-only `capabilities` projection, applied only in `handleStateCurrentGet` and `handleStateCurrentList` with the same shape as Axum `project_capabilities_for_read` and Fastify `projectAtomeCapabilitiesForRead`; the shared serializer and snapshot creation never carry capabilities, so eVe `context_menu_resolver.js` keeps its menu-access gate on iOS without adding a second server, state owner or query. Regression owner: `tests/probes/ios_state_current_capabilities.probe.mjs`.

### Mystic layer band, iOS provider relay and voice bridge (2026-09-11)

`bevy_ui_mystic_model.js` owns the Mystic's absolute stacking: the renderer puts every node on one flat scale (`GlobalZIndex(style.z_index ?? 0)`), so the tile grid carries `workspaceSceneLayerOrder('mystic')` down its whole subtree, the way `bevy_panel_tree.js` carries its own. A node left without a `z_index` is painted at 0, underneath every panel. `bevy_ui_mystic_runtime.js` owns dismissal on the native surface, where the document-level owner never sees the press: the presentation root closes on a press outside the tile grid and ignores only the reprojection of the still-held opening pointer (not released, and within `RIBBON_TOKENS.mysticOriginPressTolerancePx` of the opening point). Regression owner: `tests/eve/bevy_ui_mystic_contract.probe.mjs`.

`FastifySyncClient.reloadConfiguration` (iOS) is idempotent: the application re-publishes the same remote configuration before every authenticated request, and disconnecting on each one closed the provider channels carrying the in-flight assistant request (`provider_connection_closed`). Only a changed configuration disconnects.

`atome/src/squirrel/voice/bootstrap.js` loads its bridge modules as `{ id, path }` descriptors through `loadModulesSequentially`, so the packaged runtime resolves them by id from `__ATOME_PACKAGED_MODULES__`. The packaged bundle has no file at those paths; importing them directly failed the whole voice bridge on iOS. Regression owners: `tests/eve/voice_playback_bootstrap.test.mjs`, `tests/atome/src/squirrel/voice/bootstrap.probe.mjs`.

### Panel input sessions under the Mystic menu (2026-09-11)

`text_editing_session.js` owns whether a blur ends a session: `retainOnBlur` (stay
active, look unfocused — scene text) and `reclaimFocusOnBlur` (take the DOM focus back
— an input box with its own menu over it) are values or predicates resolved at blur
time. `bevy_panel_text_editing.js` holds its session while the Mystic it opened really
stands — the recorded field and `isMysticMenuOpen()` at blur time — released by that
menu's `onClose` or by the first blur after it is gone, including a refused opening, and
its `paste()` replaces the whole value.
`bevy_ui_pointer_runtime.js` refuses the focus to a press landing on the `mystic` layer,
which the hit result now carries from `bevy_ui_runtime.js`. `bevy_ui_mystic_runtime.js`
owns its geometry across surface changes through `subscribeRenderSurfaceSize`,
re-deriving the centre from the stored opening point, and never interrupts a close.
Root cause, evidence and rejected hypotheses:
`known-bug-solutions/ios-panel-input-fast-tap-blur/README.md`.

# Selection rail: one anchored placement for Copie and Contact — 2026-09-26

- The selection case of a list was already the canonical component: `bevy_panel_choice.js` composes `toggleableRowNode` down to `buildBevyIconButtonSurfaceNode` on the 30 px `EVE_BUTTON_SKIN_TOKENS.bevyButton` surface, and both consumers — the Copie list (`bevy_panel_selectable_list.js`) and the Contact list (`bevy_panel_contact_view.js`) — go through it. No button material, radius, tone, pressed translation or disabled opacity is re-declared in a panel.
- What did not follow the framework was the placement: each consumer wrote `position: [0, 0]`, which glued the case to the top-left corner of its row. Both ad-hoc writes are removed; a panel never places a control with a pixel of its own.
- `eVe/elements/skin/panel_skin.js` owns the rule as `listRow.selectionInsetPx` (`scalePx(3)`, i.e. the same three pixels of air the footer close disc uses), and `bevy_panel_choice.js` exports `selectionRailPosition(containerHeightPx, sizePx)` — x = inset, y = centered — as the single owner of a rail's position.
- `toggleableRowNode` gains the additive option `containerHeightPx` (default `null`): a control dropped into a taller container says so instead of placing itself, and a caller that declares nothing keeps its historical rendering unchanged. `bevy_panel_selectable_list.js` passes `resolvedRowHeight` and `bevy_panel_contact_view.js` the doubled row height, so the 60 px Copie and Contact rows centre their case with 3 px from the edge; Contact's protected own-card column reserves the same placement (`contact_select_*_protected`).
- `railRanges` now carries `railTop` (the rail's own y inside its row) and `bevy_panel_list_selection.js` reads the finger in the row's coordinates (`range.top + range.railTop + pointerY`) for both `press` and `drag`. Without that term a finger at the top edge of a doubled row answered for the row above; absent `railTop` the term is 0, so every compact consumer keeps its old bands.
